clue.text: Sporting achievement at the heart of Madrid team

indicators.note: something at the heart of another sits in its middle, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Real Madrid, the Spanish football club, is often called simply Real
a creation is something achieved or produced

explanation.surface: A sporting triumph lies at the core of Real Madrid's side.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreational activity is done for fun, as sport is, so the adjectives match in sense.

clue.text: Liberal America first to support judge's veto

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece supports the upper one, so the judge's letters sit on top
America first means the American letters are placed ahead of the Liberal letter

parts.note: a referee, or ref, judges a match
USA is the abbreviation for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A liberal America backs a judge's decision to block something.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a refusal to allow a measure, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Gangsters once discussed crack

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the Kray twins were notorious East London gangsters of the 1960s

explanation.surface: Old-time gangsters talked about a drug or a break-in.
explanation.walkthrough: The Krays, Ronnie and Reggie, ran organised crime in 1960s London; their name is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze is a network of fine cracks in a glaze or surface, so it is a kind of crack.

clue.text: Odd, Clapton covering 'Cocaine' initially before 'Money'

indicators.note: Clapton's name covers, or wraps around, the following pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: Eric Clapton is the guitarist who recorded the song Cocaine

indicators.note: before puts the cocaine letter ahead of the money piece
initially picks the first letter of the word Cocaine

parts.note: a cent is a small unit of money

explanation.surface: Eric Clapton playing his song Cocaine before a song called Money would be strange.
explanation.walkthrough: Clapton famously covered J.J. Cale's Cocaine, so 'covering' looks like a music term; it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eccentric is odd or unconventional, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Healthy prune

definitions.meaning: in good shape and lean, as a fit, slim person is
to cut back or clip, as with a hedge

explanation.definitionFit: Trim means slim and fit as an adjective, and to cut back as a verb.

clue.text: Biased? Crooked? Indeed so

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the following letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a judge is prejudiced or corrupt and gets the reply that it is so.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-sided view favours one party only, which is what biased means.

clue.text: Gleaming silver base

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
base means low, as in a low or mean act

explanation.surface: A shiny silver stand is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aglow is glowing, which is to say gleaming with light.

clue.text: Get grime out with this kitchen aid

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gadget that helps you scrub away dirt in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sand timer used for boiling eggs is a classic kitchen gadget or aid.

clue.text: Idiot anticipating trouble leading to attack

indicators.note: anticipating means coming before, so the idiot's letters go first

parts.note: an ass is a fool or idiot
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A fool expects bother that will end in an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack violently, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: In France source of happiness is right to vote

indicators.note: in places the following pieces inside the country's name

parts.note: taken as written, the country's name

indicators.note: source of takes the opening letter of the word happiness

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Being able to vote is what brings joy in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The franchise is the legal right to vote in elections, a fixed political sense.

clue.text: A good look round South African capital

indicators.note: round means the look letters go around the next pieces

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A good tour round a South African capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South African capital' wants to be read together as Pretoria or Cape Town; South is only S, leaving 'African capital'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagos was Nigeria's capital until 1991 and remains its largest city, so it is an African capital in a looser sense.

clue.text: Austrian capital's change of leadership and tone

indicators.note: the leader, or first letter, of the city's name is swapped for a different one

parts.note: Vienna is the capital of Austria

explanation.surface: Vienna changes its leaders and its mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is a reddish-brown pigment, so it is a colour tone.

clue.text: Legendary American greeting unexpected thaw within Alaska's borders

parts.note: hi is an everyday greeting

indicators.note: within puts the rearranged letters inside the border letters
borders picks the outside letters of the word Alaska
an unexpected thaw is out of the normal order, so its letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A mythical American welcomes a surprising thaw in the far reaches of Alaska.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpected' scrambles the thaw letters, and 'borders' gives the first and last letters of Alaska, which close around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiawatha is the Native American hero of Longfellow's legendary narrative poem.

clue.text: French museum opening

definitions.meaning: the great art museum in Paris that houses the Mona Lisa
a vent or slatted aperture for air or light

explanation.definitionFit: The Louvre is the Paris museum; a louvre is also a slatted opening for ventilation.

clue.text: Not of architectural interest? Not in the book

definitions.meaning: British buildings of special interest are put on an official protected list; one not on it lacks that status
not listed in a telephone directory, ex-directory

explanation.definitionFit: Unlisted describes a building without protected status and a phone number left out of the directory.

clue.text: Worker eating cold ham left sauce

indicators.note: the worker eats the next pieces, so they go inside its letters

parts.note: a worker bee is the classic crossword worker
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
taken as written

explanation.surface: A labourer ate cold ham and left the sauce behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Bechamel is a classic white sauce made from milk, butter and flour.

clue.text: Short flight, with possible danger, and land in Kent?

parts.note: a hop is a short flight, as in a quick plane trip

indicators.note: possible suggests one possible form of the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A brief trip by air, despite some risk, ends in landing in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent, a county in south-east England, is famous for growing hops for beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hop garden is a field where hops are grown, typical of Kent's countryside.

clue.text: Announcement of tea met with laughter and excitement

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out, so the tea word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a brew is a pot or cup of tea in British slang
ha-ha is the sound of laughter

explanation.surface: Calling out that tea is ready is greeted with laughs and enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy fuss or commotion, a state of excitement.

clue.text: Superior plastic or stiff paper?

definitions.meaning: a premium credit card for well-off customers
card of a gold colour, a piece of stiff paper

explanation.definitionFit: A gold card is an upmarket credit card, and literally card that is gold-coloured.

clue.text: Fade left with iron to centre of fairway? In his dreams!

definitions.text: Fade left with iron to centre of fairway? In his dreams!

parts.note: to go is to fade away or fail
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the word fairway

explanation.surface: A golfer hopes a fade struck with an iron finishes in the middle of the fairway.
explanation.walkthrough: A fade and an iron are golf terms, but here they give GO and FE; the whole clue also describes the player's hopeful shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Only a golfer dreams of shaping a fade with an iron onto the middle of the fairway.

clue.text: Give a kick to Tottenham man's leg

parts.note: Tottenham Hotspur, the London football club, are known as Spurs, so one player is a Spur
the on side, or leg side, is a cricket term for one half of the field

explanation.surface: A Tottenham footballer's limb is ready to kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg' and 'on' are interchangeable cricket terms for the side of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur on is to urge forward or give a kick, as a rider urges a horse.

clue.text: Saved money with bent teen's goods

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: gg is a short form for goods

explanation.surface: A corrupt teenager's possessions represent their savings.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is a sum of money put aside for the future.

clue.text: Rich drunkard reported to have debts

parts.note: a lush is a heavy drinker
IOUs are written promises to repay, so having debts means holding out IOUs

explanation.surface: A wealthy heavy drinker is said to owe money.
explanation.walkthrough: Say LUSH followed by IOUS and you hear the answer; the SH sound is written SC in the grid word.
explanation.definitionFit: Luscious food is rich and sweet in taste, so the adjectives overlap.

clue.text: Popular half-sister in Bury

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: half here takes the second half of the word sister

explanation.surface: A well-liked stepsister lives in the town of Bury.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury a body in a grave, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Touch inattentive with the French nowhere to be found

parts.note: careless means inattentive
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An absent-minded touch that has lost its French connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A caress is a gentle loving touch, and as a verb means to touch tenderly.

clue.text: Boredom an element in umpteen nuisances

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Tedium is part of dealing with endless annoyances.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French borrowing for listlessness or weariness, the same feeling as boredom.

clue.text: Calamari — tip not included — for a pound

indicators.note: the tip, or first letter, is left out of the word for calamari

parts.note: calamari is squid served as food

explanation.surface: A plate of calamari costs a pound, service excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip not included' reads like a restaurant bill; it means drop the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Quid is British slang for a pound sterling.

clue.text: The ultimate opening episode

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so the final letter of the word The is taken

parts.note: a vent is an opening for air or smoke

explanation.surface: The final opening episode of a series.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence or happening, as an episode is.

clue.text: One Parisian in outbreak of bad acne is plenty

indicators.note: in puts the French word for one inside the rearranged letters
an outbreak scatters things, so the letters of bad acne are rearranged

parts.note: un is French for one, as a Parisian would say

explanation.surface: A Parisian with a fierce eruption of acne has plenty of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outbreak of' scrambles the bad acne letters, and 'in' sets the French one among them, so a Parisian is just the French language signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance means a great quantity, the same as plenty.

clue.text: Street performance rearranged in back garden

indicators.note: rearranged tells you the following letters are put in a new order
